title: Projects Architecture
summary: define Project folder-link projection, three-way Project State ownership, targeted refresh, resolver lookup generation, and local access isolation
content_html:
Projects Architecture

Purpose

This document is the implementation reference for the Projects feature. It defines how folder links enter documents, how the Projects customisation projects them, how Project State reconciles three independent inputs, and how Resolver Tokens consume one bounded generated lookup.

The governing flow is:

current folders -----------+
Project document manifest -+-> Project State snapshot -> report data
canonical Studio Works ----+                         \-> Project resolver lookup

explicit Resolver Token -> exact keyed lookup -> one-hop rendered groups

No arrow grants mutation authority over an input.

Authorities

concern authority
local path containment and existence exact targets confined below $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/
Project discovery and seed inventory configured discovery roots, initially $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/projects/
Work source-path snapshot canonical Studio Work record
Work-to-Series membership canonical Studio catalogue
Project notes and membership document source in dotlineform/projects
literal convenience target optional Project document folder_path front matter
normalized manifest projection and Projects controls registered Manage-only Projects sub-scope customisation
reconciliation model, report payload, and Project resolver lookup Docs Viewer Project State producer
resolver capability definition and access small global Docs Viewer resolver-definition registry
rendered Resolver Token result document builder reading one declared lookup row

Studio Boundary

folder_path and project_folder are not aliases. folder_path belongs only to Project document source and the namespaced Docs Viewer Manage manifest. PRJ-1 local links and PRJ-2 metadata/seeding add no Studio field, UI control, read path, write path, or service dependency.

Project State has one explicit integration seam because Studio owns the historical evidence it reconciles. PRJ-3 reads existing Work/Series data and uses the Studio-read-only server-side post-commit Work observer described below to refresh the derived Docs Viewer snapshot. The observer writes Project State only. It never writes folder_path, rewrites project_folder, changes the catalogue transaction, or makes a successful Work commit contingent on Project State follow-through.

Project Document Data Contract

folder_path is an optional normalized POSIX path relative to $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/:

folder_path: "projects/3 symbols"

The configured dotlineform/projects collection selects a known Projects customisation. Its controlled projector adds the value only to the exact row's namespaced local management data:

{
  "doc_id": "d-example",
  "title": "3 symbols",
  "customisation": {
    "folder_path": "projects/3 symbols"
  }
}

The default manifest fields, public manifest, and public browser descriptor do not gain folder_path. Missing, malformed, duplicate, or non-resolving values remain reportable states and never alter document membership.

The Projects Edit Metadata contribution reads and writes the field only for an explicit validated {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} target. Creation and bulk seed use the same normalizer and exact-target document writer.

Local Path Contract

The shared parser accepts:

  • local file: URLs;
  • absolute POSIX paths with ordinary spaces; and
  • absolute POSIX paths whose characters are backslash-escaped for shell display.

Input is parsed as data. There is no shell evaluation, environment-variable or home expansion, command substitution, relative-path resolution, remote file authority, or non-file: scheme.

Normalization strips the configured root and produces one decoded base-relative POSIX target plus an encoded link representation. Body Markdown uses dlf-local:projects/3%20symbols; structured metadata stores only projects/3 symbols. The Projects feature supplies $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/ as its allowed root. Metadata may save a non-existing contained target; activation requires the target to exist. A local Open in Finder service receives the exact relative target, resolves and reconfines it below that base root, and never falls back to a displayed document, parent collection, title, or URL text from a different target.

Containment and discovery are separate policies. Links and folder_path may target any contained folder. Automatic Project candidate discovery scans only configured Project discovery roots, initially projects/; it does not recurse through Docs Viewer scopes, configuration, or every other directory merely because they share the same base root.

PRJ-1 renders dlf-local: links as clickable only in local Manage. Public projection recognizes the explicit marker and retains a safe inert label or placeholder while removing the marker and target. General redaction and verification of absolute paths authored as prose, raw HTML, or code is a separate public-build delivery.

Project State Inputs And Model

A full Project State refresh reads:

configured Project discovery inventory
    + exact existence checks for declared base-contained targets
    + current dotlineform/projects Manage manifest
    + current canonical Works
    -> normalized relationship snapshot

Folder keys are normalized relative paths below $DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR/, so an ordinary project key begins with projects/ and an explicitly linked folder elsewhere remains representable. Work folder evidence is derived from project_folder plus optional project_subfolder and normalized into that same base-relative namespace; project_filename is not part of folder topology. The model retains incomplete and unmatched evidence instead of discarding it.

The same snapshot atomically publishes:

  • the read-only Project State report payload; and
  • the Manage-only Project resolver lookup.

The report is hosted by one ordinary report document in scope dotlineform. It links to exact Project documents, Works, Series, and validated folder targets. It owns no repair action.

Resolver Contract

Resolver addressability is global, but relationship data is not one global graph. A small code-owned definition registry declares:

  • resolver ID and access level;
  • accepted subject kinds and key normalization;
  • lookup location and schema version; and
  • ordered result groups.

Each resolver's domain producer owns its generated lookup. Project State is the only producer of the Project lookup. Rows are precomputed for exact folder and Work subjects, carry snapshot generation metadata, and contain only the declared one-hop groups:

folder -> Works[] + Project documents[]
Work   -> folders[] + Project documents[]

Expansion parses the exact resolver and subject, enforces access, loads that single lookup, performs one exact-key read, and renders the row's groups in configured order. There is no fuzzy match, contextual fallback, canonical registry scan, or traversal from returned items.

Within the initial resolver, Works sort by normalized Work ID, Project documents by title then doc_id, and folders by normalized relative path. A missing or stale lookup produces an explicit unavailable state rather than a live scan.

Refresh And Mutation Contract

Full Refresh

A full refresh reads all three inputs and atomically replaces the complete report and resolver snapshot. It runs when:

  • the Project State report opens or the user chooses explicit Refresh;
  • the snapshot is missing, corrupt, or version-incompatible;
  • a mutation cannot supply trusted before/after data; or
  • the user explicitly requests Rebuild All.

Direct Finder changes have no reliable application event and become visible at the next full refresh. That refresh scans configured discovery roots and checks exact declared contained targets; it does not inventory the entire base directory indiscriminately. A filesystem watcher is not part of the initial contract.

Targeted Update

Known committed changes use exact deltas and recompute only affected subject and reverse-membership rows. A compact JSON lookup may still be atomically rewritten; that is not a logical full rebuild when relationship computation was confined to the supplied delta.

Examples include:

  • Work create/delete: add or remove the exact Work subject and affected folder rows;
  • Work folder change: update the Work row and the union of old/new folder rows;
  • Work title change: update result labels that display that Work;
  • Work series_ids change: update report enrichment without adding a Resolver Token Series edge; and
  • Project folder_path change/delete: update the document row and its old/new folder reverse memberships.

Batch mutations with complete before/after records publish one targeted multi-record generation.

Exact Studio-Read-Only Observer

The Work observer runs at the server-side committed mutation boundary and is read-only with respect to Studio. It is not a browser Save event, media upload event, or publication status transition. The Work editor currently calls POST /studio/api/catalogue/work/save; work_save_payload() holds current_record, updated_record, and changed_fields around the canonical works.json transaction.

After a successful canonical commit, one Project State impact classifier uses those exact values:

field class fields effect
folder topology project_folder, project_subfolder targeted Work and old/new folder update
rendered Work label title targeted displayed-link update
report enrichment series_ids targeted report update only
irrelevant project_filename, status, dates, other metadata no Project State update

Work create, save, delete, bulk save, and import paths call the same classifier. Browser code never decides whether to rebuild Project State.

This is the only new Studio integration in Projects. It responds to the existing canonical fields after commit and writes derived Docs Viewer data; it grants Docs Viewer no mutation authority over Studio.

Failure And Freshness

If post-commit Project State follow-through fails, the Work or Project document remains committed. The previous complete snapshot is retained and marked stale; the response reports a derived-projection failure and must not cause the source mutation to repeat.

Relationship freshness and rendered-document freshness are separate:

input mutation -> Project State snapshot update
document rebuild -> rendered Resolver Token list update

Project State does not silently rebuild every document containing a Resolver Token. A future dependent-document refresh would require its own explicit usage index and bounded workflow.

Retirement Boundary

Project State moves completely out of Studio. Delivery removes or reroutes /studio/project-state/, its report/open endpoints, frontend, activity contract, Markdown generator/opener, focused tests, and var/studio/reports/project-state.md.

The new folder inventory observes folder identity only. The old primary-image audit is not retained implicitly. IMAGE_EXTENSIONS currently has another catalogue consumer, so reusable policy must move to a neutral owner before the old report module is deleted.

Architectural Invariants

  • There is no canonical Project-folder registry.
  • Project State has one Docs Viewer owner and one generated snapshot.
  • Report and resolver data come from the same normalized generation.
  • Targeted updates are the default for trusted application mutations; full refresh is the explicit fallback and filesystem-observation path.
  • Resolver expansion has depth one and never refreshes its lookup.
  • Local folder data and activation do not enter public projections.
  • Projects does not implement a general public-content path redactor or public private-path verifier.
  • No relationship result authorizes mutation of a Work, document, Series, or folder.

The Projects Concept defines the product model. The Local File And Folder Links Concept owns the reusable target and link contract. The feature parent owns delivery order.
